subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned and can move to an SE deep-dive / proposal: 

Key pain points you shared
- Inference unit economics: current per-request cost is too high for scale; primary ask is to reduce cost per inference by ~2x while preserving quality.
- Latency sensitivity: customer-facing features need p95 < 200ms for short text completions.
- Ops overhead: managing self-hosted GPUs and tuning quantization is time-consuming for your infra team.

Current stack and constraints (as discussed)
- Self-hosted on AWS (single-node p3.2xlarge today) running a 7B open model behind an internal API.
- Some float16 quantization already in use; open to more aggressive quantization if quality preserved.
- Need SOC2 evidence and PCI considerations for payment flows (we noted this for procurement).

Success criteria for a POC
1) Demonstrate >= 2x reduction in per-unit inference cost at comparable latency and quality for the 7B workload.
2) Maintain p95 latency < 200ms for representative request distribution.
3) Clear operational playbook (autoscaling/batching/caching + rollout plan).

Proposed next steps
- I’ll attach a preliminary Dedicated pricing sheet and a short POC scope doc for your review (attached).
- Schedule an SE deep-dive next week to go through tokenization, batching expectations, and quantization trade-offs — Ben will lead that.
- You confirm stakeholders and procurement timeline so we can include procurement in the loop.

Open questions I captured
- Typical request size & tokens per call (we have an estimate of ~45 tokens avg; please correct if off).
- Spike patterns during batch jobs vs. real-time requests.
- Any hard constraints on model variants we must support (e.g., can’t downgrade from current model family).

Thanks — I’ll wait for a quick confirmation on timing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing summary), Redwood_POC_mvp_scope.docx (POC scope)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finbot.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches what I captured. A few clarifications and answers to your open questions: 

- Tokens per call: our current avg is ~42 tokens (short prompts + completion). Peak bursts during end-of-month reports can triple traffic for short windows.
- Current model: We’re running a tuned 7B Llama-variant (float16) in-house; we’re open to INT8/4 quantization if you can show minimal quality regression on our test prompts.
- Latency target is correct: p95 < 200ms; for a subset of low-latency flows we’d like p50 < 100ms.
- SOC2: procurement indicated they need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short data handling summary for the POC. I’ve CC’d procurement.
- Budget & timeline: we can commit to a 3-week POC starting the week of 2026-05-04. Ballpark budget for proof-of-value is $60k.

Next steps for us: please send a short mutual action plan and proposed SE deep-dive agenda. Also include any pre-POC checklist (VPN, sample dataset transfer, non-prod access).

On the quantization openness: we’re comfortable testing INT8, but would like to see a quality baseline beforehand. Batching/caching: we expect batching to help but are nervous about tail latency — if you have examples of prefix caching reducing cost without latency regressions that would be helpful to show.

Thanks — looking forward to the SE session.

Best,
Alex Turner
Head of ML, FinBot
alex.turner@finbot.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-3221

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finbot.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex —

Great — I’ll run the SE deep-dive and propose this agenda:
1) Review current token distribution and sample prompts (15 min)
2) Baseline latency & throughput expectations on your sample workload (20 min)
3) Batching & KV/prefix caching strategy for short completion flows (20 min)
4) Quantization plan: INT8/4 tradeoffs and quick quality eval approach (20 min)
5) POC logistics: access, SOC2/PII handling, success metrics (15 min)

Can you confirm availability for a 90-minute session the week of 2026-04-27? If that doesn’t work, Marissa — maybe the week of 05-04 per their start preference for the POC.

I’ll also bring a short demo showing 2x unit-cost reductions on a comparable 7B workload using batching + INT8 on similar hardware.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
